A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same work and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and appendices A–B. The retained material can be matched across section moves and renumbering.

before.justification: V1 reports original graph simulations, empirical scaling-law validation, CORA depth experiments, and node-classification results for the proposed models.

after.justification: V2 retains those original experiments and adds ogbn-ArXiv results and activation/filter ablations. Baseline results attributed to other papers are distinguishable from the proposed models' results.

M1.justification: The activation substitution, bifurcation-aware initialization, and shared/per-layer polynomial filters are retained. V2 Section 5.2 reorganizes the Sine-Poly models already described in v1 Section 6.2; the additional activation variants are experimental controls.

E1.justification: V2 adds large-scale ogbn-ArXiv node classification in Table 1. The original eleven benchmarks, synthetic graph families, grid example, and CORA depth scenarios remain.

E2.justification: The comparison set substantially expands through GCN + PairNorm in Table 1 and unfiltered Sine GCN plus shared/per-layer GELU-Poly and Swish-Poly controls in Table 6. PairNorm was named in v1 but had no reported comparison scores. The original evaluated comparators remain.

E3.justification: V2 introduces ranking methods by accuracy within each dataset and averaging ranks across benchmarks excluding ogbn-ArXiv. The original 60/20/20 splits, 50-configuration search, search ranges, and training procedure remain stated unchanged. No separate ogbn-ArXiv protocol is provided.

E4.justification: V1 compared Sine-Poly with ReLU-Poly. V2 Section 6.3 and Tables 2, 5, and 6 substantially extend this analysis by removing polynomial filtering and testing GELU and Swish, addressing whether gains depend on filtering or the particular activation. The original depth and initialization-sensitivity analyses remain.

E5.justification: V2 adds standard deviations of ranks across datasets in Tables 2 and 5, introducing a cross-dataset dispersion summary. Both versions retain accuracy reporting as mean ± standard deviation over ten runs; the PDFs do not establish an increase in runs.

E6.justification: V2 adds ogbn-ArXiv, PairNorm, alternative-activation, unfiltered-model, and aggregate-ranking results. In corresponding Table 1 entries, ReLU-Poly(A)-sh on Wisconsin changes from 82.27 ± 0.1 to 86.27 ± 0.1. V2 also contains unexplained differences between Tables 1 and 6, including Sine-Poly(A)-sh on Texas at 85.59 versus 90.09; these cannot be interpreted as established performance gains.

T1.justification: V2 corrects Taylor-expansion factors in Equation 4 and the multidimensional proof, changes Theorem A.1's activation assumption from C to C³, and adds a continuous-time perturbation derivation in Appendix A.1. The central bifurcation, NTK, and initialization results remain.

C1.justification: The abstract and central contributions remain. However, v2 removes the introduction's explicit assertion of substantially improved 64-layer performance and expressly qualifies the conclusion's theoretical analysis as local, modestly tempering the main claims.

C2.justification: V2 interprets the new ablations as showing that polynomial filtering is important for benchmark performance and that activation substitution alone produces results resembling vanilla GCN. It also explicitly acknowledges the analysis's locality. The existing fixed-topology limitation is retained.

D1.justification: V2 supplies a code-repository URL, discloses selected depth and polynomial order by model and dataset in Table 4, and explicitly identifies the depth experiment as using GCN without spectral filtering. These are documentation additions; the appendix still retains its future-release statement.

R1.justification: V2 adds the GELU and Swish references supporting its new comparisons. The Stuart-Landau citation retains the same work title with revised bibliographic information, rather than introducing a different research direction. The broader positioning remains unchanged.

P1.justification: V2 expands the introduction and experimental overview, moves the polynomial-model description into Section 5.2, adds Section 6.3 and an introductory appendix subsection, and updates cross-references. These are targeted organizational and explanatory revisions; most text remains intact.

P2.justification: Table 1 is expanded, reordered, and relocated. New tables display selected hyperparameters, ablation accuracies, and rank summaries; Table 2 partly repeats Table 5. The original dataset-statistics table is retained as Table 3, and Figures 1–5 remain substantially unchanged. Visual changes are concentrated in the tabular presentation.

improvement.justification: The added controls help distinguish activation and filtering contributions, while selected hyperparameters, code pointers, and mathematical corrections improve documentation. The gain is limited by unexplained discrepancies between v2 Tables 1 and 6, including the Texas Sine-Poly result, and insufficient detail about the added ogbn-ArXiv evaluation. Overall, v2 offers useful additional evidence and clarity without substantially resolving the work's remaining weaknesses.
